ordered_diagnoses: Papillary urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential

s1.syndrome_frame: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
Calcific specks in the bladder lesion
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound showed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks in the bladder
Lesion demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement in the early arterial and venous phases
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion showing heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Endometriosis of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy and presence of a bladder lesion

shortlist.label: Polypoid cystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound and CT findings of a polypoidal lesion in the bladder

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential
shortlist.why_kept: Bladder lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a bladder lesion with calcific specks and patient's symptoms of hematuria and dysuria

raw.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on CT, along with hematuria and dysuria, is most consistent with a malignant process such as urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Endometriosis of the bladder
rejected.why: While endometriosis can cause bladder symptoms, the imaging findings of a well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks are not typical for endometriosis.

rejected.label: Polypoid cystitis
rejected.why: Polypoid cystitis is a benign condition that typically presents with multiple small lesions, not a single large lesion as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Papillary urothelial neoplasm of low malignant potential
rejected.why: While this diagnosis is possible, the presence of calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on CT makes urothelial carcinoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Malacoplakia
rejected.why: Malacoplakia is a rare condition that typically presents with multiple small lesions, not a single large lesion as seen in this case, and often has a distinct appearance on imaging with calcifications.
